leakage_notes: Rule thresholds and weights are declared, or fitted on development rows only.
The challenger is fitted on development rows only and its threshold variant is tuned on development rows only.
Validation and holdout metrics are produced from the same frozen configuration list, so they are comparable but not independent of the search.

results.description: Majority-direction benchmark: every evaluable day called bullish.
Minority-direction benchmark: every evaluable day called bearish.
one-day dollar momentum benchmark: follow the trailing return's sign.
one-day dollar mean-reversion benchmark: fade the trailing return's sign.
five-day dollar momentum benchmark: follow the trailing return's sign.
five-day dollar mean-reversion benchmark: fade the trailing return's sign.
twenty-day dollar momentum benchmark: follow the trailing return's sign.
twenty-day dollar mean-reversion benchmark: fade the trailing return's sign.
Single-rule arm: One-day dollar continuation, the lookback the live F5 already uses.
Single-rule arm: Weekly dollar continuation, slower than the live one-day threshold.
Single-rule arm: The counter-hypothesis: weekly dollar mean reversion. Kept so the registry contains the opposite bet.
Single-rule arm: Position relative to the 20-observation mean.
Single-rule arm: The live F1 regime mapping: high VIX is a dollar haven bid.
Single-rule arm: Direction of the VIX move rather than its level.
Single-rule arm: Relative rather than absolute risk level, so the rule travels across volatility regimes.
Single-rule arm: Credit spreads widening is a stress signal independent of equity volatility.
Single-rule arm: Higher US front-end yields raise the dollar's carry; the live F2 threshold is 5bp and is treated as provisional.
Single-rule arm: The engine's own F3 idea: the spread change is the relative-rate signal, not either leg alone.
Single-rule arm: German front-end moves read through EUR weakness, which lifts the dollar index.
Single-rule arm: Long-end US yield change as a lower-weight term-premium proxy.
Single-rule arm: The live F4 idea with a wider provisional threshold.
Single-rule arm: Slower real-yield trend, so the rule is not a duplicate of the five-day version.
Single-rule arm: Belly of the real curve, closer to the policy path than the 10Y.
Single-rule arm: Inflation-compensation change, kept at low weight because its sign is genuinely ambiguous.
Single-rule arm: Dovish repricing (falling 2Y) is expected to weaken the dollar; realised front-end change is the proxy for the priced path.
Single-rule arm: Monthly policy repricing, less sensitive to single data prints.
Single-rule arm: The 3M bill trading above the effective rate is the market pricing hikes; below it, cuts.
Single-rule arm: Repo funding pressure has historically produced a dollar bid; low weight because episodes are rare.
Single-rule arm: The live F6 mapping: gold strength is read as dollar weakness.
Single-rule arm: Equity risk-on is expected to soften the dollar (the live F10 mapping at a longer lookback).
Single-rule arm: EUR weakness is the dominant weight in the broad dollar index, so it is a confirmation input rather than new information.
Single-rule arm: Energy strength is treated as a global-growth signal, which is dollar supportive.
